ESTER: Polyester film and specialty polymer maker (Haryana). Q1 FY27 results approved 11 Aug; earnings call 18 Aug. Caution: trailing-twelve-month figures show a loss of ~₹27.5cr on ₹1,375cr revenue, with a low interest-coverage ratio flagged, and the stock is down ~4% over a year. Recent quarters showed a turnaround (recycled PET scaling, film utilisation improving), but this is the weakest balance sheet on the list — the chart is ahead of the fundamentals here.
MAZDOCK: Zero-debt defence-shipbuilding PSU. FY26 revenue +12%, and Q1 FY27 PAT jumped ~21% with margins expanding; analysts point to a long order book and a healthy net-cash position. Rich valuation is the main risk.
CONCOR: Navratna PSU, India's largest container-rail logistics operator. Q1 FY27 standalone PAT +7.7% to ₹277.6cr; consolidated roughly flat YoY on revenue of ₹2,160cr. The bright spot is volume — throughput +8.9% to 14.04 lakh TEUs — while pricing competition keeps earnings flat. Double-stacking on the new WDFC-JNPA line is the structural catalyst. Declared ₹1.60 interim dividend. Stock still well below year-ago levels.
UNIONBANK: PSU bank, and the cleanest fundamental story on this list. Q1 FY27 standalone PAT +29.5% to ₹5,332cr, gross NPA down to 2.65% from 3.52% YoY, net NPA 0.47%, capital adequacy 18.46%, provision coverage ~95%. The catch is growth: deposit growth of ~3.5% badly trails the 8-9% guidance and credit growth of 12.5% is below target, so profit is coming from asset-quality improvement more than expansion.
SEAMECLTD: Offshore marine services (diving support, vessel charter) for oil and gas. Market cap ~₹3,905cr, up ~93% over the past year; TTM revenue ₹952cr, profit ₹254cr, promoter holding 72.7%. Recent news: a USD 9.42mn diving agreement with HAL Offshore, and vessel SEAMEC SWORDFISH off-hired from 30 July for planned maintenance. Note: reported Q1 FY27 figures differ materially across secondary sources — verify against the company filing before relying on the quarter. Trades at ~3x book; tax rate looks unusually low.
APLAPOLLO: India's largest branded structural steel tube maker, second globally, and net-cash (₹1,410cr). Q1 FY27 PAT +11% to ₹263cr on revenue +8% to ₹5,607cr — achieved despite volumes falling 6% to 744,823t, as management chose margin over volume and lifted EBITDA per tonne 18% to ₹5,522. Volume miss driven by UAE geopolitics and an India energy crunch; July volumes rebounded 20% MoM. Management reaffirms 20% EBITDA growth for FY27. Decade record: 15% volume CAGR, 28% profit CAGR.
BLS: Visa and consular outsourcing plus digital services, on a net-cash balance sheet of ₹1,617cr. Record quarter: Q1 FY27 revenue +25.3% to ₹891cr, EBITDA +23.6% to ₹252cr at a 28.3% margin, PAT +11.4% to ₹202cr. Visa and consular grew 21.6% with segment margins above 40%; digital grew 32.2%. Profit lagged revenue mainly because the effective tax rate rose from 9.6% to 14.4%. Subsidiary BLS E-Services closed the Atyati Technologies acquisition in July. Stock sits ~35% below its 52-week high.
FINKURVE: Tech-first gold-loan NBFC operating as Arvog; RBI-registered, middle-layer, non-deposit-taking. Q1 FY27 AUM +134.5% YoY to ₹1,270cr, PAT +65.8% to ₹8.4cr, branches up to 118 from 83, active gold-loan customers +61% to 31,522. Gross NPAs low at 0.54%, and a Godrej Finance co-lending tie-up adds funding. Caveat: a small, fast-levering lender — finance costs and leverage are rising alongside AUM, so growth at this speed carries real credit risk if gold prices or collections turn.
